outputs.L1: An oil supply structure for a planetary gear device includes: a planetary gear device having a tubular body that rotates together with a carrier supporting planetary gears, the tubular body having a lubricating oil introduction port formed therein; an annular body that slides against the tubular body and has a lubricating oil supply passage communicating with the lubricating oil introduction port; a pair of seal rings attached to either the tubular body or the annular body on opposite axial sides of the lubricating oil introduction port; bypass passages that bypass the respective seal rings; and a pair of pressure-reduction mechanisms disposed either between the lubricating oil introduction port and the respective seal rings or outside the respective seal rings, each pressure-reduction mechanism limiting the flow of lubricating oil between the tubular body and the annular body.
outputs.L3:
The oil supply structure is designed for use in a planetary gear device having a carrier that rotatably supports a plurality of planetary gears. A tubular body is configured to rotate together with the carrier and includes a lubricating oil introduction port through which lubricating oil is supplied to the planetary gear device.

An annular body is arranged in sliding contact with the tubular body. The annular body includes an oil supply passage that communicates with the lubricating oil introduction port, thereby allowing lubricating oil to flow from the annular body into the rotating tubular body.

A pair of seal rings is disposed on opposite axial sides of the lubricating oil introduction port. These seal rings help restrict leakage of lubricating oil from the interface between the tubular body and the annular body. Bypass passages are provided around the respective seal rings to establish alternative flow paths for the lubricating oil.

The structure further includes two pressure reduction mechanisms that restrict the flow of lubricating oil between the tubular body and the annular body. These pressure reduction mechanisms may be positioned axially inside the pair of seal rings, toward the lubricating oil introduction port, or axially outside the seal rings. By limiting oil flow and reducing pressure near the sealing regions, the mechanisms support reliable lubrication while helping control leakage and improve the durability of the sliding and sealing components.
outputs.L4:
An oil supply structure is provided for lubricating a planetary gear device having rotating components that require a stable and controlled supply of lubricating oil. The structure includes a rotating tubular body connected to or formed as part of the planetary gear device and a stationary annular body disposed around the tubular body. An oil port formed in the stationary annular body communicates with a corresponding oil port in the rotating tubular body as the tubular body rotates, thereby defining an oil supply path from a stationary oil source to the interior of the planetary gear device.

A pair of seal rings is arranged between the stationary annular body and the rotating tubular body on opposite axial sides of the oil ports. The seal rings define an annular oil chamber that maintains fluid communication between the ports despite relative rotation of the two bodies. Oil introduced into the annular chamber passes through the port in the tubular body and is delivered to bearings, gear meshes, pinion shafts, or other portions of the planetary gear device requiring lubrication.

The structure further includes one or more restricted passages around the seal rings. These restrictions limit the amount of oil that can flow from the annular chamber toward adjacent spaces. By controlling such flow, the structure maintains an appropriate lubricating pressure while reducing unnecessary leakage and preventing excessive oil from reaching regions in which it could increase drag, churning loss, or heat generation.

Bypass passages are also provided to establish alternative flow paths around selected portions of the sealing arrangement. If pressure rises in the annular chamber or near one of the seal rings, oil can escape through a bypass passage rather than acting directly on the seal ring. The bypass passages may communicate with a lower-pressure region, a drain space, or another portion of the lubrication circuit. Their dimensions and locations can be selected so that normal lubrication flow is preserved while excessive local pressure is relieved.

Pressure-reduction mechanisms may be incorporated into the bypass passages or associated oil paths. Such mechanisms can include throttling portions, grooves, orifices, enlarged chambers, stepped passages, or combinations of these features. As oil passes through them, its pressure is progressively reduced before it reaches a seal-adjacent or drain region. This arrangement limits pressure differences across the seal rings and reduces the likelihood that a ring will deform, lift from its sealing surface, wear unevenly, or permit an excessive amount of oil to pass.

The paired seal rings, restricted leakage paths, bypass passages, and pressure-reduction mechanisms therefore cooperate to regulate the transfer of oil between the stationary and rotating bodies. Oil needed for operation of the planetary gear device is supplied reliably through the aligned ports, while flow around the seals is kept within a controlled range. At the same time, pressure that might otherwise accumulate near the seal rings is diverted and reduced.

As a result, the oil supply structure improves lubrication control within the planetary gear device, decreases seal-related leakage, and helps protect the seal rings from excessive pressure loading. The design can also reduce oil consumption, frictional loss, heat generation, and deterioration of sealing performance, thereby contributing to improved efficiency, durability, and reliability of the planetary gear device.
outputs.L5:
### An Oil Supply

Oil supply refers to the amount of crude oil available for production, transportation, and consumption. Oil is extracted from underground reserves and offshore fields, then transported to refineries where it is turned into fuels and other products. A stable oil supply is important for transportation, industry, electricity generation, and the global economy.

However, oil supplies can be affected by wars, political decisions, natural disasters, equipment failures, and changes in demand. When supply decreases, oil and fuel prices often rise. Many countries therefore maintain emergency oil reserves and seek different suppliers to improve energy security. At the same time, governments are investing in renewable energy to reduce dependence on oil and limit its environmental impact.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract describing an oil supply structure for a planetary gear device with a rotating tubular carrier body, an annular sliding body, seal rings, bypass passages, and pressure-reduction mechanisms.
counterfactuals.output: An oil supply structure for a planetary gear device includes a tubular carrier body rotatable about an axis, an annular sliding body disposed around the carrier body, and seal rings arranged between the carrier body and the sliding body to define an annular oil supply chamber. Pressurized oil introduced into the oil supply chamber is supplied through an oil passage in the carrier body to a lubrication target of the planetary gear device. At least one bypass passage communicates a region of the oil supply chamber with a lower-pressure region outside the oil supply chamber. A pressure-reduction mechanism, including at least one of a throttling portion, a pressure-reducing groove, or a pressure-responsive valve, is provided in the bypass passage or adjacent to a seal ring. The pressure-reduction mechanism reduces pressure acting on the seal ring and discharges oil accumulated between sealing portions, thereby suppressing seal-ring deformation, sliding resistance, oil leakage, and heat generation while maintaining an oil supply to the planetary gear device.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an invention for supplying oil to planetary gears, including a carrier-mounted tubular body, an oil supply passage, paired seals, seal-bypassing passages, and paired flow-restriction mechanisms.
counterfactuals.output:
An oil-supply device for planetary gears includes a tubular body fixed to and rotating with the planet carrier. The tubular body defines an oil-supply passage that receives lubricant from a stationary or upstream supply and directs it toward the planetary-gear bearings and meshing portions.

A pair of axially spaced seals is arranged between the tubular body and an adjacent oil-delivery member to limit leakage. Separate seal-bypassing passages extend around the respective seals, providing controlled alternative flow paths rather than allowing oil to pass uncontrolled through the sealing interfaces. Each bypass passage is equipped with a corresponding flow-restriction mechanism. The paired restriction mechanisms meter the bypass flows, maintain suitable pressure in the main oil-supply passage, and prevent excessive leakage while permitting lubrication and pressure equalization under different operating conditions.

This arrangement reliably supplies oil to the rotating planetary gears while reducing seal wear, oil loss, and pressure fluctuations.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Convert the following engineering concept into formal patent language: a planetary gearbox receives lubricant through a rotating tube and sliding annular member, with seals on both axial sides of the inlet and bypass/restriction features that reduce oil flow.
counterfactuals.output: A lubrication arrangement for a planetary gearbox comprises a rotatable lubricant-supply tube and an annular member disposed about the lubricant-supply tube. The annular member is axially slidable relative to the lubricant-supply tube and defines, in cooperation therewith, a lubricant inlet communicating with one or more lubrication passages of the planetary gearbox. First and second sealing elements are disposed on respective, axially opposite sides of the lubricant inlet to inhibit leakage from the inlet. The lubrication arrangement further comprises a flow-control structure including at least one bypass passage, flow restriction, or combination thereof, configured to reduce a quantity of lubricant delivered through the lubricant inlet to the planetary gearbox.
